To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the infectivity of aerosolized tularemia bacilli decreased more rapidly than their viability, the decrease in infectivity was more rapid in man and the monkey than in mice or guinea pigs, the decrease in respiratory infectivity for the monkey was more rapid than that for man, and the respiratory infectivity of the bacilli was diminished after 2 hr in all four species of host.
the respiratory infectivity of aerosolized P. tularensis decreased more rapidly than viability in aging aerosols, and that the infectivity was reduced 10 times after 3 hours of exposure in monkeys.
the airborne infectivity of P. tularensis is reduced 10-fold in 3 hours.
